tasks.title: F3: route ResetViewport's zoom write through ZoomLevelGuard and pin the guard property the reset relies on
acceptance: Every production assignment to `FloorMapDrawable.ZoomLevel` under src/DungeonMaster.App takes its value from `ZoomLevelGuard.Next(...)`, and that includes the zoom write `ResetViewport` performs, whether directly or by calling `ApplyZoom`. This is the backlog row's requirement itself (.sir/backlog.md line 196 as read at Gate 1: 'Route ResetViewport ... through ZoomLevelGuard, so every zoom write shares the non-finite guard'). Evidence: `grep -rnE "ZoomLevel[[:space:]]*(=([^=]|$)|\+=|-=|\*=|/=)" src/DungeonMaster.App --include=*.cs --exclude-dir=obj --exclude-dir=bin`, every hit read by eye (a right-hand side continuing on the next line is read there). At startRef it printed exactly 2 hits: DungeonDetailPage.xaml.cs:520 (`= ZoomLevelGuard.Next(_drawable.ZoomLevel, raw);`) and :527 (`= 1.0f;`, unguarded), so this criterion fails at startRef. Must-match case: the startRef :527 line. Near miss that must not match: `_drawable.ZoomLevel * 100` (startRef :521). Second count: `grep -n ZoomLevel src/DungeonMaster.App/Views/DungeonDetailPage/DungeonDetailPage.xaml.cs` classified by eye, write versus read; the two counts must agree. The property declaration initializer `{ get; set; } = 1.0f;` in FloorMapDrawable.cs is a default, not an assignment, and is not matched.

Preserved: after `ResetViewport` returns, `_drawable.ZoomLevel` is 1.0f, `_drawable.PanOffset` is `PointF.Zero`, `ZoomPercentLabel.Text` is "100%", and `MapCanvas.Invalidate()` has been called at least once. Evidence: read from source. The zoom value follows from `ZoomLevelGuard.Next(current, 1.0f)` returning 1.0f for every `current`, per ZoomLevelGuard.cs:43-53 at startRef (1.0f is finite, lies inside the snap band, and is inside [0.25, 4.0]). If the label is now computed as `$"{(int)Math.Round(_drawable.ZoomLevel * 100)}%"` (the ApplyZoom route), it evaluates to "100%" for 1.0f.

Preserved (F2, decided by the user at Gate 1: accept as-is): the `case '0':` block in DungeonDetailPage.xaml.cs that calls `ResetViewport()` only under `KeyChord.IsControlOnly(e.Modifiers)` (startRef :484-488) is unchanged. Evidence: the diff the reviewer is handed shows no change to those lines.

src/DungeonMaster.App.Tests/Views/ZoomLevelGuardTests.cs gains a test asserting `ZoomLevelGuard.Next(float.NaN, 1.0f)` returns exactly 1.0f: the guard property `ResetViewport` now relies on to bring a non-finite level back to 100%. This deliberately pins behaviour the guard already has at startRef; what it preserves is that a reset routed through the guard recovers a corrupted level. Its name states the condition and the outcome (test discipline, Naming: 'A test name states the condition and the expected outcome').

That test is shown able to fail (test discipline, Coverage: 'A test is shown able to fail'). Demonstrated discrimination, at one site: at src/DungeonMaster.App/Views/DungeonDetailPage/ZoomLevelGuard.cs:43, replace `if (!float.IsFinite(raw))` (it occurs once in the file; `grep -c 'IsFinite' ZoomLevelGuard.cs` prints 1 at startRef) with `if (!float.IsFinite(raw) || !float.IsFinite(current))`. Then run `dotnet test C:/dm-wt/20261103-2239-app-follow-ups/src/DungeonMaster.App.Tests/DungeonMaster.App.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~ZoomLevelGuardTests"`. The new test fails (Expected 1, Actual NaN). Revert. Report the injected text, the command, its printed summary, and the revert.

A second new test, the control, asserts `ZoomLevelGuard.Next(ZoomLevelGuard.MaximumZoom, 1.0f)` returns exactly 1.0f. It passes under the same injection, shown in the same filtered run, so the injected failure is the non-finite-current case and not a broken apparatus. The 7 tests ZoomLevelGuardTests.cs held at startRef (`grep -cE "^[[:space:]]*\[Fact\]"` prints 7) also pass under the injection.

src/DungeonMaster.App/Views/DungeonDetailPage/ZoomLevelGuard.cs ends byte-identical to startRef. The task owns it only for the injection window. Evidence: `sha256sum` of the file before the injection and after the revert, both quoted in the report, are equal. The revert is verified before any solution-wide build.

Every file this task edits remains all-CRLF with zero lone CR. Evidence: `perl -0777 -ne '$cr=()=//g; $crlf=()=/
/g; $lf=()=/
/g; print "$cr $crlf $lf
"' <file>` prints three equal numbers for DungeonDetailPage.xaml.cs, ZoomLevelGuardTests.cs and ZoomLevelGuard.cs (each was all-CRLF with 0 lone CR at startRef). Control, run once in the task's scratch directory: a fixture written with `printf 'a
bc
'` must print `2 1 2`. Use tabs for indentation in .cs files (dm-conventions dotnet-format.md). Never `sed -i`, never `Write` an existing file, and never end an Edit's new_string on whitespace.

After the revert is verified, `dotnet build C:/dm-wt/20261103-2239-app-follow-ups/src/DungeonMaster.sln` succeeds and its summary reads `0 Warning(s)` and `0 Error(s)`; quote both lines. Then `dotnet test C:/dm-wt/20261103-2239-app-follow-ups/src/DungeonMaster.sln --no-build` reports zero failures and prints a total for each of the three test assemblies. The DungeonMaster.App.Tests total equals the total that assembly printed before this task's first edit plus the number of tests this task added; quote both totals.
